issues.description: ID generation using component-scoped variable 'nextId' will reset on every re-render. This causes duplicate IDs and state corruption when todos are added, as nextId resets to 1 on each render cycle.
issues.suggestion: Use useState or useRef to persist the ID counter across renders: const nextIdRef = useRef(1); const addTodo = (data: Omit<Todo, 'id' | 'completed'>) => { setTodos([...todos, { ...data, id: nextIdRef.current++, completed: false }]); };

issues.description: Todos filtering and sorting runs on every render, including when unrelated state changes (like search input). This creates unnecessary re-computation, especially with large todo lists.
issues.suggestion: Memoize the filtered and sorted todos using useMemo to only recalculate when dependencies change.

issues.description: Array.sort() mutates the original array. Since filteredTodos is derived from the todos state array, this can cause unexpected mutations and violate React's immutability principle, potentially breaking state updates.
issues.suggestion: Create a shallow copy before sorting to avoid mutation: const sortedTodos = [...filteredTodos].sort((a, b) => { ... });

issues.description: The search state is passed to TodoList component but never actually used in the filtering logic. Search input changes but has no effect on displayed todos, creating a confusing UX bug.
issues.suggestion: Implement search filtering in the filteredTodos computation.

issues.description: Inline arrow functions in onToggle and onDelete are recreated on every render, causing TodoList to re-render even when todos haven't changed.
issues.suggestion: Extract handlers using useCallback to maintain referential equality.

codeQuality.summary: The component has a critical bug with ID generation that will cause duplicate IDs and state corruption. High severity issues include array mutation during sorting and missing search functionality implementation. Performance can be significantly improved with useMemo and useCallback hooks.

untestedPaths.reasoning: The 'active' filter branch filters todos to show only incomplete items. This is core functionality that users rely on.

suggestions.description: The 'nextId' variable is declared inside the component function but outside state management. This will be reset to 1 on every re-render, causing ID collisions and data corruption.
suggestions.benefits: Prevents ID collisions and ensures each todo gets a unique, incrementing ID. Using useRef preserves the value across re-renders without triggering additional renders.

suggestions.description: The filtering and sorting logic is complex and should be extracted into a custom hook or separate functions with useMemo.
suggestions.before: const filteredTodos = todos.filter(...).filter(...); const sortedTodos = filteredTodos.sort(...);
suggestions.benefits: Improves code organization, testability, and maintainability. Using useMemo prevents unnecessary recalculations when unrelated state changes.

suggestions.description: Inline arrow functions in JSX props are recreated on every render, causing unnecessary re-renders of child components.
suggestions.after: const handleToggle = useCallback((id: number) => { setTodos(prevTodos => prevTodos.map(...)); }, []); const handleDelete = useCallback((id: number) => { setTodos(prevTodos => prevTodos.filter(...)); }, []);
suggestions.benefits: Prevents unnecessary re-renders of TodoList component by maintaining stable function references. Improves performance, especially with larger todo lists.

refactorings.summary: The App.tsx file has several critical issues. The most critical is the 'nextId' variable bug which will cause ID collisions - this must be fixed using useRef. The component also suffers from performance issues due to inline callbacks and non-memoized computations. Extracting the complex filtering/sorting logic would significantly improve testability and readability.

issues.description: Date comparison logic flaw: Comparing Date objects with < operator compares timestamps, but 'new Date()' includes time component. A due date set to today will fail validation if current time has passed midnight, even though the date itself is valid.
issues.suggestion: Compare only the date portions, ignoring time: const today = new Date(); today.setHours(0,0,0,0); const selectedDate = new Date(dueDate); selectedDate.setHours(0,0,0,0); if (selectedDate < today) { ... }

issues.description: Invalid date handling: new Date(dueDate) with an invalid date string returns 'Invalid Date' object which doesn't throw an error but produces NaN timestamp. Comparison with < returns false, allowing invalid dates to pass validation.
issues.suggestion: Validate date string before comparison using isNaN(date.getTime()).

issues.description: Potential XSS vulnerability through unvalidated user input: The 'text' field accepts arbitrary user input without sanitization. While React escapes content by default when rendering, if this data is passed to components that use dangerouslySetInnerHTML or stored in backend without sanitization, it creates XSS risk.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation and length constraints (maxLength attribute, text.length > MAX_LENGTH check).

issues.description: Missing input attributes for accessibility and security: Input fields lack 'maxLength', 'autoComplete', 'required', and ARIA attributes. Missing maxLength allows unlimited input that could cause DoS through oversized payloads.
issues.suggestion: Add security and accessibility attributes: maxLength={500}, required, autoComplete="off", aria-label, aria-invalid.

suggestions.description: The handleSubmit function contains validation logic, form submission, and state reset. These responsibilities should be separated into dedicated validation and reset functions for better testability.
suggestions.before: const handleSubmit = (e: React.FormEvent) => { e.preventDefault(); if (!text.trim()) { ... } if (dueDate && new Date(dueDate) < new Date()) { ... } onAdd(...); setText(''); ... }
suggestions.after: const validateForm = (): string | null => { ... }; const resetForm = () => { ... }; const handleSubmit = (e: React.FormEvent) => { e.preventDefault(); const validationError = validateForm(); if (validationError) { setError(validationError); return; } onAdd(...); resetForm(); }
suggestions.benefits: Improves testability by allowing validation logic to be tested independently. Reduces cyclomatic complexity. Makes the code more maintainable and adheres to single responsibility principle.

suggestions.description: The date comparison creates new Date objects inline and doesn't account for time component. Should use more explicit date comparison logic.
suggestions.after: const isDateInPast = (dateString: string): boolean => { const selectedDate = new Date(dateString); const today = new Date(); today.setHours(0,0,0,0); selectedDate.setHours(0,0,0,0); return selectedDate < today; };
suggestions.benefits: Provides more accurate date comparison by normalizing time components. Improves code readability and reusability. Prevents edge cases where same-day tasks are incorrectly flagged as past due.

suggestions.description: The type assertion 'priority as Todo['priority']' is a code smell. The priority state should be properly typed from the start.
suggestions.before: const [priority, setPriority] = useState('medium'); onAdd({ text, priority: priority as Todo['priority'], dueDate });
suggestions.after: type TodoPriority = 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'; const [priority, setPriority] = useState<TodoPriority>('medium'); onAdd({ text, priority, dueDate });
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates unsafe type assertion. Provides better IDE autocomplete. Prevents invalid priority values at compile time.

refactorings.summary: The TodoForm component has 8 refactoring opportunities spanning validation extraction, state management consolidation, type safety improvements, and accessibility enhancements. issues.description: Function 'getPriorityColor' accepts 'string' type but only handles specific values ('high', 'medium', 'low'). The priority parameter should be strictly typed to prevent runtime bugs and ensure type safety.
issues.suggestion: Define a union type for priority values: type Priority = 'high' | 'medium' | 'low'; const getPriorityColor = (priority: Priority): string => { ... }

issues.description: Potential XSS vulnerability: 'todo.text' is rendered directly without sanitization. If user input is not sanitized on the server side, malicious scripts could be executed.
issues.suggestion: Ensure 'todo.text' is sanitized server-side or use a sanitization library. React's default XSS protection should handle this for text content, but verify data validation at the API/database layer.

issues.description: Inline arrow function in onChange creates a new function instance on every render, causing unnecessary re-renders of child components and potential performance issues in large lists.
issues.suggestion: Use useCallback to memoize the handler: const handleToggle = useCallback(() => onToggle(todo.id), [onToggle, todo.id]);

issues.description: Date object is instantiated on every render even if 'todo.dueDate' hasn't changed. This creates unnecessary object allocations.
issues.suggestion: Memoize the formatted date: const formattedDueDate = useMemo(() => todo.dueDate ? new Date(todo.dueDate).toLocaleDateString() : null, [todo.dueDate]);

issues.suggestion: Add date validation and error handling with try-catch and isNaN(date.getTime()) checks.

issues.description: Filter operation executes on every render without memoization. In a component that re-renders frequently, this causes unnecessary re-computation of the filtered list even when 'todos' or 'search' haven't changed.

suggestions.after: const filterTodosBySearch = (todos: Todo[], search: string): Todo[] => { const searchLower = search.toLowerCase(); return todos.filter((todo) => todo.text.toLowerCase().includes(searchLower)); }; const visible = filterTodosBySearch(todos, search);

suggestions.description: The component uses a simple filter that recalculates on every render. Using React.useMemo would optimize performance by memoizing the filtered results.

suggestions.description: The filtering logic is a UI concern mixed with data transformation. Consider implementing a custom hook (useFilteredTodos) that encapsulates the filtering logic and memoization.
suggestions.after: const useFilteredTodos = (todos: Todo[], search: string) => { return React.useMemo(() => { if (!search) return todos; const searchLower = search.toLowerCase(); return todos.filter((todo) => todo.text.toLowerCase().includes(searchLower)); }, [todos, search]); }; const visible = useFilteredTodos(todos, search);

recommendations.description: Fix ID generation bug in App.tsx: The nextId variable resets on every render, causing duplicate IDs and data corruption. Use useRef to persist the counter across renders.

Implement search functionality in App.tsx: The search state is declared but NOT used in the filtering logic. Users can type in the search box but it has no effect. Add search filtering to the filteredTodos computation.
Add comprehensive test coverage: All 5 files have 0% test coverage. Priority: Test the search filter logic (core feature), date validation, and form submission flows before merging.
Fix date validation in TodoForm.tsx: The date comparison includes time components, causing today's date to fail validation. Normalize dates to midnight before comparison.
Add memoization to prevent unnecessary re-renders: Use useMemo for expensive filtering/sorting operations and useCallback for event handlers in App.tsx, TodoList.tsx, and TodoItem.tsx.
Add input validation and sanitization: The text field accepts unrestricted input without length limits. Add maxLength attributes, validate input length, and ensure server-side sanitization.
Fix array mutation in App.tsx: Array.sort() mutates the original array, violating React's immutability principles. Create a shallow copy before sorting.
Improve TypeScript type safety: Extract TodoPriority type, add runtime type guards for validation, use Date type instead of string for dueDate, and eliminate unsafe type assertions.
Add ARIA labels and semantic HTML: Interactive elements lack proper labels for screen readers. Add aria-label, aria-invalid, and role attributes throughout components.
Refactor for maintainability: Extract utility functions (getPriorityColor, date formatters), use custom hooks for filtering logic, and add comprehensive JSDoc documentation.
